title: Can AI Coach an Athlete? My Two-Week Touch Rugby Training Plan
text:
Introduction




My Touch Team!!


Touch rugby is one of those sports most people in the United States have never heard of, but the rest of the world absolutely loves. It is especially big in Australia and New Zealand, where people grow up playing it the way kids here grow up playing basketball or soccer. The easiest way to describe it is that it is a version of rugby without tackling. Instead of getting taken to the ground, play stops with a simple touch. Think of it as tag with a ball, except everyone is sprinting, passing, stepping, and trying to outsmart each other at full speed. It looks simple until you try it, and then you realize how technical and exhausting it actually is.
In two weeks, I will be attending a three-day touch rugby training camp as part of my preparation for USA Nationals with the NYC team. The camp runs from eight in the morning to four in the afternoon and each day is packed with drills, attacking lines, defensive patterns, footwork, conditioning, sprint work, and constant ball handling. It will be the most intense stretch of touch rugby training I have done so far, and I want to make sure I am actually ready for it.
Two weeks is not a lot of time to prepare, and I did not want to show up to camp feeling unprepared. So instead of randomly picking workouts or hoping practices would be enough, I asked an LLM to help me create an actual training plan. I wanted something realistic that matched the speed, movement, and ball-handling demands of touch rugby. This post includes the prompt I used, the plan the AI created, and my first impressions before I try it out.

Prompt:

I have a three-day touch rugby camp in two weeks. Each day runs from eight in the morning to four in the afternoon with constant movement including drills, sprinting, defensive structures, attacking lines, gameplay, agility work, conditioning, footwork, and ball handling. Please design a training plan to help me get ready. Include a realistic two-week training schedule, specific conditioning workouts for agility, sprint speed, and endurance, strength preparation focused on core stability, lower-body strength, and injury prevention, daily recovery recommendations, nutrition and hydration guidance for long training days, and mental preparation strategies that support confidence, game awareness, and fast decision-making. Make the plan tailored to the demands of touch rugby specifically.



Response:

Absolutely! Preparing effectively for a three-day touch rugby camp requires a smart, well-rounded two-week plan that targets the physical, mental, and tactical demands of the sport. Below, you’ll find a tailored 14-day approach focused on:

🧠 Mental Prep & Game Awareness

- Mentally rehearse touch defense resets

Look at elite touch games (YouTube)

👟 Final 3 Days Before Camp

Replace full lifts with bodyweight mobility
Sleep extra

Pack gear/snacks/sunscreen early
Feel sharp, not tired
✨ Summary of Priorities
✅ Sprint Speed – Short burst acceleration
✅ Agility – Directional changes under fatigue
✅ Endurance – Game-specific high-intensity intervals
✅ Strength – Lower body, core, injury prevention
✅ Skills – Ball handling, game patterns, reactive play
✅ Recovery – Mobility, foam rolling, sleep
✅ Nutrition – Carb and protein-focused recovery meals
✅ Mindset – Visualization, decision-making, confidence
You’ll show up faster, sharper, more resilient—and most importantly—mentally ready to perform across all three days. Good luck with camp—dominate it! 🏉🔥

title: A Random Shower Thought: How Much Does Birth Order Affect Who You Become?
text:
Introduction:
This whole post started because I had a random thought in the shower. There are so many stereotypes about oldest, middle, youngest, and only children, and people repeat them like they are universal truths. The more I thought about it, the more I realized something funny: almost all of my closest friends are second children. I never planned that and it just kind of naturally happened. So I started wondering if that was a coincidence or if there is an actual reason I gravitate toward people with that kind of sibling dynamic.
That made me curious about whether birth order actually shapes who we become or if it is just something we like to joke about because it feels relatable. I wanted a clearer explanation, not from TikTok or from random personality memes, but from something that could break down the theories and the research behind it, so I turned to an LLM to help me understand it.

title: A Random Shower Thought: How Much Does Birth Order Affect Who You Become?
text:
Prompt:

Explain whether birth order actually affects personality. Include classic theories and what modern research says. Make it easy to understand. text:
Response:
Sure! Let’s talk about birth order and personality in a simple and clear way.

title: A Random Shower Thought: How Much Does Birth Order Affect Who You Become?
text:
The Big Question:
Does your order in the family (oldest, middle, youngest, or only child) shape your personality?

Classic Theories
Years ago, psychologists like Alfred Adler (a student of Freud) were among the first to suggest that birth order matters. According to these early theories:

Oldest children are responsible leaders because they had to take care of younger siblings.
Middle children are peacemakers and feel overlooked, so they become social and adaptable.
Youngest children are outgoing, attention-seeking, and sometimes rebellious.
Only children are mature for their age, perfectionists, and sometimes loners because they got all the attention — and pressure — from adults.

These ideas became very popular and are still around in books, articles, and even jokes today.



What Modern Research Says
However, modern science is more cautious.
Large studies involving thousands or even millions of people in recent years show that: - Birth order has little to no consistent effect on broad personality traits such as extraversion, agreeableness, conscientiousness, neuroticism, or openness. - Any differences that do show up tend to be very small and may disappear entirely when controlling for things like family size, income, or age gaps.
That said, some research has still found specific patterns — especially related to intelligence and behavior, not core personality.



What Might Be True — and Why
Here’s a comparison of typical birth order traits — and whether there’s solid evidence to back them up:









Birth Order
Common Beliefs
Backed by Research?
Notes




Oldest
Responsible, organized, leadership skills, high achievers
🟡 Partially
Firstborns may score slightly higher on IQ and school achievement. Could be a result of more attention early on.


Middle
Adaptable, peacekeepers, feel “in the middle”
🔴 Weak evidence
These traits are hard to prove scientifically and may depend more on family context.


Youngest
Funny, outgoing, attention-loving, risk-takers
🔴 Weak evidence
This might describe some youngest kids, but it’s not reliable across the board.


Only Child
Mature, perfectionist, self-sufficient, lonely?
🟡 Somewhat
They often behave like firstborns, and the “lonely only” myth is not well supported.



So, while some patterns seem tomake sense, they’re not strong enough to predict personality in all cases.



Why Do These Ideas Persist?
People love patterns — and families are full of stories.

Parents may treat kids differently depending on birth order, which affects their experiences — though not always their deep personality.
Stereotypes can stick and become “self-fulfilling.” For example, if everyone tells the youngest they’re the clown, they might lean into it.
Culture and media reinforce these beliefs — think of the bossy big sister or the spoiled youngest in TV shows.




Why You Might Click with People of a Certain Birth Order
Interestingly, we may feel more comfortable with people whose birth order matches or complements ours. Why?

Shared experience: Firstborns might relate to other firstborns because they both had to “grow up quickly.”
Balance: A middle child may enjoy a relationship with an only child who craves connection, balancing out each other’s needs.
Familiarity: Some people are simply drawn to people who remind them of their own siblings — for better or worse!




In Summary

Birth order can influence experiences, but it doesn’t strongly shape your personality overall.
Some small effects show up (like intelligence in firstborns), but personality traits are mostly shaped by many things: genes, parenting, environment, culture, and even chance.
Still, the concept of birth order resonates with people because families are emotional, personal experiences — and labels can help us understand ourselves.

So, birth order might affect how you see yourself or how others treat you, but it probably doesn’t define who you truly are.

title: My New Gaming Mastermind: An LLM
text:
Introduction:
Lately my roommates and I have been playing a lot of CATAN, and I finally admitted to myself that I have no idea what I’m doing. I place my settlements wherever looks “fine,” hope for good rolls, and somehow always end up stuck without the resources everyone else has. So I figured it might be fun to see whether an LLM could actually make me better at the game.
For this post, I treated the AI like a strategy coach. I had it ask me a few questions about how I usually play and what I struggle with, and then I let it build a plan for how I should think about placements, trades, and long-term strategy. title: My New Gaming Mastermind: An LLM
text:
Prompt:

I’ve been playing CATAN with my roommates and want to get better at the game. Before you give me any advice, ask me three to five questions about how I usually play, where I struggle, what decisions I make during setup, and what my overall playstyle is. After I answer, give me specific strategies tailored to my habits. Include guidance on starting placement, resource balance, trading, expansion timing, road building, and how to adapt depending on the board. Keep the advice practical and something I can actually use in my next game.


Getting to Know My Play Style:

What’s your primary goal when you sit down to play? I’m still new, so I mostly try to collect as many resources as possible. I usually start with roads and place settlements wherever I can.


What do you look for in your first two settlement placements? I try to get a mix of resources. I don’t understand numbers very well yet, so I focus on brick, wheat, wood, and ore.


Where do you usually fall behind? I’m often still waiting on the right resource mix just to build my next settlement.


What’s your usual approach to trading? I’m not a strong trader. I don’t hoard on purpose—I just never have the right cards. I mainly trade with players and forget about ports and bank trades.

title: My New Gaming Mastermind: An LLM
text:
Response:
Okay, this gives me a fantastic picture of your current playstyle! It’s very common for new players to focus on just collecting resources and building roads, and struggling with the “right mix” for expansion.
Here’s some practical, actionable advice tailored to your habits, designed to help you break through those bottlenecks and start playing more strategically:


Tailored Strategies for Your Catan Game
Your main challenge seems to be transitioning from simply collecting resources to building a reliable resource engine that allows you to expand and score points. Let’s tackle that!

1. Starting Placement: Beyond Just a Mix, Think Engine
You’re right to prioritize a mix of resources, but let’s refine that with the “number strategy.”

Understand the Numbers (Probability):

The numbers on the resource hexes correspond to the probability of rolling that number with two dice.
Most Likely: 6 and 8 (5 out of 36 chance each)
Next Most Likely: 5 and 9 (4 out of 36 chance each)
Less Likely: 4 and 10 (3 out of 36 chance each)
Least Likely: 3 and 11 (2 out of 36 chance each), 2 and 12 (1 out of 36 chance each)
Actionable Tip: When choosing your first two settlements, prioritize spots that have at least two high-probability numbers (6s, 8s, 5s, 9s) under them. A spot on a 6, 8, and 5 is gold! A spot on a 2, 12, and 3 is very risky.

Focus Your Engine for Early Expansion:

Your goal is to build settlements (1 Wood, 1 Brick, 1 Wheat, 1 Sheep). To do this reliably, you need a strong production of these four.
First Settlement: Aim for a spot that gives you strong Wood and Brick production (to build roads) AND strong Wheat/Sheep (for the settlement itself). A good starting combo might be:

Spot 1: High-probability Wood, Brick, and Wheat. (e.g., 6 Wood, 8 Brick, 5 Wheat)
Spot 2 (on your return pick): High-probability Sheep, and ideally another high-probability of one of the previous three (Wood, Brick, Wheat) to bolster your engine. This ensures you have all four settlement resources covered with decent odds.

Avoid “Spread Too Thin”: Don’t try to get every resource with your first two placements if it means sacrificing high-probability numbers. It’s better to have strong production of 3-4 key resources and trade for the rest, than weak production of all 5.




2. Resource Balance & Expansion Timing: Break the “Waiting” Cycle
You mentioned often waiting for the right mix of resources. This is where a focused engine and proactive trading come in.

Identify Your Next Goal, Then Your Resource Needs: Instead of just “collecting as many resources,” ask yourself: “What do I want to build next?”

If a Settlement: You need 1 Wood, 1 Brick, 1 Wheat, 1 Sheep.
If a City: You need 2 Wheat, 3 Ore.
If a Development Card: You need 1 Wheat, 1 Sheep, 1 Ore.

Actionable Tip: Prioritize Settlements Early. A new settlement gives you 1 point and, crucially, starts producing resources from that new hex. This rapidly accelerates your engine. Don’t build roads aimlessly; build them towards a specific, valuable new settlement spot.
The “2 Roads, 1 Settlement” Cycle: A common and effective early game strategy is to build two roads to reach a new settlement spot, then build the settlement. This means your engine needs to reliably produce: (1 Wood + 1 Brick) for the first road, then (1 Wood + 1 Brick) for the second road, then (1 Wood + 1 Brick + 1 Wheat + 1 Sheep) for the settlement. If you can get this cycle going, you’ll expand rapidly.



3. Trading: Be Proactive, Not Just Reactive
This is a game-changer for new players! You’re currently waiting for the right things or for others to offer. Let’s flip that.

Actionable Tip: Announce Your Needs and Offers Aggressively.

“I need X for Y.” Instead of “Anyone have Wheat?”, try “I need a Wheat for a settlement, who can help?” This tells people your goal and might make them more willing to trade.
“I’ll trade Z for X.” If you have 3 Wood and need a Wheat, say “I’ll give 2 Wood for 1 Wheat!” (Start high, you can always go down). Or “I have plenty of Ore, who needs Ore?”
Don’t Be Afraid to Overpay Slightly (Early Game): If you need one specific resource to complete a settlement and get your engine going, giving up two of something you have in abundance for one of what you desperately need is often worth it. That new settlement will pay for itself!

Don’t Forget Ports!

Actionable Tip: Identify Your Port Resource. If you’re sitting on a hex that produces a lot of one resource (e.g., you have two settlements on Sheep hexes), try to get to the Sheep port (2:1 trade). This effectively makes your abundant resource twice as valuable!
General 3:1 Port: If you don’t have a specific resource port, try to build to a 3:1 port. This is always better than the 4:1 bank trade.
When to Use Ports: Use them when other players aren’t offering what you need, or when you have a huge surplus of one resource that no one wants. It’s often better than letting cards sit in your hand and potentially getting robbed.

Bank Trades (4:1):

Actionable Tip: Last Resort, But Don’t Forget It! If you have 8 Wood and desperately need 1 Ore, and no one will trade, and you’re not on a port, turn in 4 Wood for 1 Ore. It’s inefficient, but sometimes it’s the only way to make a build happen.




4. Road Building: Strategic Pathways, Not Just “Wherever Possible”
Your current approach of “roads first and then settlements wherever it seems possible” can be inefficient.

Actionable Tip: Build Roads with a Purpose.

Identify Target Spots: Look for future settlement spots that are on high-probability numbers, give you a new resource, or connect to a port.
Block Opponents: If an opponent is clearly trying to reach a prime spot, sometimes building a road to block them is more valuable than placing a settlement immediately.
Longest Road: Don’t chase Longest Road too early unless your starting placement naturally allows for it. Settlements are worth points and resources. Longest Road is just points. Focus on settlements first.




5. Adapting to the Board & Opponents

Resource Scarcity/Abundance:

Actionable Tip: At the start of the game, look at the board. If there’s very little Sheep, Sheep will be valuable! If there’s tons of Wood, it will be less valuable unless someone needs it for Longest Road. Plan your trades and placements accordingly. If Sheep is scarce, getting a reliable Sheep source is key for settlements and dev cards.

The Robber:

Actionable Tip: Protect Your Engine. If you have a settlement on a 6 Ore and an 8 Wheat, that’s your engine! If an opponent rolls a 7, they will likely place the robber on one of those spots. Try to spread out your vital resources across different numbers if possible.
Robber Placement (When You Roll a 7): Always place the robber on the highest-producing number of the player who is currently in the lead or is your biggest threat. Take the resource they likely need most. Don’t just place it randomly.

Watch Your Opponents:

Actionable Tip: Pay attention to what resources your opponents are collecting and what they are building.

If someone is hoarding Wheat and Ore, they’re probably going for cities.
If someone is building a lot of roads, they need Wood and Brick.
This intel helps you with trading (“I know they need Wood, so I can ask for more for it!”) and robber placement.




Your Next Game Checklist:

Initial Placement: Focus on 2-3 high-probability numbers (6s, 8s, 5s, 9s) for your first two settlements. Ensure you have a strong production of Wood, Brick, Wheat, and Sheep.
Goal-Oriented Building: Ask “What do I want to build next?” (Settlement, City, Dev Card) and identify the specific resources you need.
Proactive Trading: Announce your needs and offers. Don’t just wait. “I need 1 Wheat for a settlement, who has it?”
Ports: If you have an abundance of one resource, identify a port to build towards. Use 3:1 or 2:1 ports before 4:1 bank trades.
Strategic Roads: Build roads with a purpose – to reach a specific, valuable new settlement spot, or to block an opponent.

You’ve got this! Catan is all about building an efficient engine and making smart trades. By focusing on these points, you’ll see a significant improvement in your ability to expand and score points. Good luck!

title: Can AI Build a Trip My Family Will Actually Enjoy?

title: Can AI Build a Trip My Family Will Actually Enjoy?

After creating the main itinerary, produce two additional versions. One should be more food oriented and highlight restaurants and bars. The other should be more focused on cultural sites, holiday activities, and scenic locations. Keep both versions clear, realistic, and easy to follow.
Finally, evaluate all versions of the itinerary. Point out anything that may not make sense for winter or for our budget and suggest adjustments that would make the trip smoother.

title: From Taipei to Philadelphia: Asking AI Where a 20 Something Belongs
text:
Prompt:

I’m in my early twenties, about to graduate, and trying to figure out where I should live next. title: From Taipei to Philadelphia: Asking AI Where a 20 Something Belongs
text:
Response:

This is a fantastic question, and your background in both Taipei and Philadelphia gives you a unique perspective! You’ve experienced very different urban environments, which will help you appreciate the nuances of other cities. I’ll rank around 10 cities that offer a great balance for someone in their early twenties, focusing on the criteria you mentioned. “Affordability” is always relative, especially in global cities, so I’ll consider it in comparison to other major hubs.


Top Cities for Early-Twenties Graduates
1. Berlin, Germany Why it’s a great fit: Berlin is a magnet for young people due to its unique blend of history, vibrant arts scene, and burgeoning tech industry. It’s relatively affordable compared to other major European capitals, especially for rent. The social scene is incredibly diverse, with countless bars, clubs, cafes, and cultural events. Public transport is excellent, and the city is very bike-friendly. There’s a strong international community, making it easier to meet people. Job opportunities are growing, particularly in startups and tech. The food scene is varied and affordable, and safety is generally high. Key Strengths: Culture, affordability (relative), social life, public transport, job opportunities (tech).
2. Lisbon, Portugal Why it’s a great fit: Lisbon has exploded in popularity, and for good reason. It offers an incredibly high quality of life at a more affordable price point than many Western European cities. The city is stunning, with a vibrant social scene, delicious food, and a warm climate. There’s a growing tech and startup ecosystem, attracting many young professionals. Walkability is high (though hilly!), and public transport is good. The community feel is welcoming, and it’s easy to meet people, especially with the influx of expats. Dating and friendships thrive in its relaxed atmosphere. Key Strengths: Affordability (relative), social life, culture, food, climate, growing job market.
3. Toronto, Canada Why it’s a great fit: Toronto is a truly multicultural metropolis with a robust economy and diverse job opportunities across many sectors (finance, tech, media, healthcare). It’s incredibly safe, has excellent public transportation, and boasts a vibrant social scene with endless options for food, nightlife, and culture. While not cheap, it offers a higher earning potential than some European cities. It’s very walkable in many neighborhoods, and the community is highly welcoming to newcomers and international residents. Key Strengths: Job opportunities, diversity, safety, public transport, social life, culture.
4. Melbourne, Australia Why it’s a great fit: Consistently ranked among the world’s most livable cities, Melbourne offers an exceptional quality of life. It’s renowned for its arts, culture, food, and coffee scene. Job opportunities are strong, especially in finance, healthcare, and tech. The city is very walkable, with an extensive tram network. It has a lively social scene, great community feel, and a strong emphasis on outdoor activities. While rent can be high, salaries are generally competitive. Key Strengths: Quality of life, culture, food, job opportunities, safety, public transport.
5. Amsterdam, Netherlands Why it’s a great fit: Amsterdam offers a fantastic quality of life, especially for young people. It’s incredibly international, with a large expat community, making it easy to meet people. The city is beautiful, very safe, and highly walkable/bikeable with excellent public transport. Job opportunities are good, particularly in tech, creative industries, and international business, and many companies operate in English. The social scene is vibrant, and there’s a strong emphasis on work-life balance. The main drawback is the high cost of living, especially for housing. Key Strengths: Quality of life, international community, safety, walkability/biking, job opportunities, culture.
6. Chicago, USA Why it’s a great fit: For a major US city, Chicago offers a surprisingly good balance of job opportunities, culture, and relative affordability (compared to NYC or SF). It’s a major hub for finance, tech, healthcare, and manufacturing. The city has stunning architecture, world-class museums, a fantastic food scene, and passionate sports culture. Public transport is decent, and many areas are walkable. The social scene is lively, and it’s easier to build a community than in some other large US cities. Safety varies by neighborhood, but generally improving in core areas. Key Strengths: Job opportunities, affordability (relative for US), culture, food, public transport (for US).
7. Montreal, Canada Why it’s a great fit: Montreal offers a unique blend of North American dynamism and European charm. It’s significantly more affordable than Toronto or Vancouver, making it very attractive for recent graduates. The city is bilingual (French and English), which adds to its cultural richness. It has a thriving arts and music scene, excellent food, and a vibrant nightlife. Job opportunities exist, particularly in tech, gaming, aerospace, and creative industries. Public transport is efficient, and the city is very walkable. It has a strong community feel, especially within its distinct neighborhoods. Key Strengths: Affordability (relative for NA), culture, food, social life, unique vibe, public transport.
8. Singapore Why it’s a great fit: If career growth, safety, and efficiency are top priorities, Singapore is hard to beat. It’s a global hub for finance, tech, and logistics, offering abundant high-paying job opportunities. The public transportation system is world-class, and the city is incredibly safe and clean. Food is a national obsession, with hawker centers offering delicious and affordable meals. There’s a large expat community. The main downsides are the extremely high cost of living (especially housing and cars) and a potentially more structured social scene compared to some Western cities. Key Strengths: Job opportunities, safety, public transport, food, efficiency, cleanliness.
9. Barcelona, Spain Why it’s a great fit: Barcelona offers an incredible lifestyle with beautiful architecture, fantastic food, a vibrant nightlife, and proximity to beaches and mountains. It’s very walkable, with good public transport. The social scene is lively, and there’s a strong sense of community. While the cost of living is rising, it’s still relatively affordable compared to Northern European capitals. The main challenge for a recent grad might be job opportunities, especially if you don’t speak Spanish or Catalan, and salaries can be lower. However, it’s a great place for cultural immersion and enjoying life. Key Strengths: Lifestyle, culture, food, social life, walkability, climate.

It’s very safe, and there’s always something happening, from K-pop concerts to traditional markets. Job opportunities are strong in tech, media, and design, especially if you have specialized skills or Korean language proficiency. It offers a unique cultural experience and a fast-paced environment. The main challenges can be the language barrier if you don’t speak Korean, and the job market can be competitive for foreigners without specific in-demand skills or a strong network. Key Strengths: Culture, food, safety, public transport, technology, dynamism.


Which cities might match someone who grew up in Taipei?
Someone who grew up in Taipei would likely appreciate cities that share some of its characteristics: Efficient and extensive public transportation: Taipei’s MRT is excellent. High safety: Taipei is very safe. Vibrant and diverse food culture: Street food and diverse dining options are key. High density and walkability: A compact, easy-to-navigate urban environment. Strong work ethic and modern infrastructure: A sense of progress and efficiency. Cleanliness and order (relative to other cities).
Cities that might resonate with a Taipei background: 1. Singapore: This is probably the closest match. It shares Taipei’s hyper-efficiency, incredible safety, world-class public transport, and a fervent food culture (especially hawker centers). It’s also very clean and modern, with a strong emphasis on career progression. 2. Seoul, South Korea: Shares the high-tech integration, incredibly efficient public transport, high safety, and a dynamic, youth-driven culture with fantastic food. The urban density and constant activity would feel familiar. 3. Amsterdam, Netherlands: While culturally very different, it shares the excellent public transport, high safety, and a very bike-friendly, dense urban environment where things generally work efficiently. 4. Melbourne, Australia: While not as dense as Taipei, it has a strong food culture, excellent public transport (trams!), and a high quality of life with a sense of order and cleanliness.


Which cities feel closer to Philadelphia?
Someone who studied in Philadelphia might appreciate cities that share some of its characteristics: Distinct neighborhoods with unique identities: Philly is known for its diverse neighborhoods. Historical significance and a sense of “grit” or authenticity: A less polished, more real urban feel. Strong sports culture: Philly fans are passionate. Walkable areas but also reliance on cars in some parts: A mix of urban and suburban accessibility. A strong sense of local community within a larger city. North American urban structure and lifestyle.

It also offers a similar blend of historical significance and modern urban life, with a strong sense of local identity. 2. Montreal, Canada: While bilingual, Montreal shares a similar historical depth, distinct neighborhood feel, and a strong sense of local culture. It has a more European flair but still operates within a North American context, offering a unique blend that might resonate. 3. Toronto, Canada: As a major North American city, Toronto shares the diverse population, a strong economy, and a similar urban structure to many US cities. While perhaps less “gritty” than Philly, its diverse neighborhoods and strong community feel would be familiar.


I hope this detailed breakdown helps you narrow down your choices! Each city offers a unique experience, and your personal priorities will ultimately guide your decision. Good luck with your graduation and your next big adventure!

title: AI, Tell Me I’ll Be Okay
text:
Introduction
Finals week is stressful — papers, exams, deadlines, and not enough sleep. Every student has their own way of coping, but I wanted to test something different: can large language models (LLMs) act like a supportive therapist during one of the most stressful weeks of the semester?
In this post, I asked three different LLMs the same question to see which one sounded the most like a real therapist.

title: AI, Tell Me I’ll Be Okay
text:
LLM 1: ChatGPT-4o

Absolutely, I’m here for you. First, I want to say—it’s completely okay to feel overwhelmed during finals week. You’re facing a lot of pressure, and that stress is a natural response. But you’re not alone, and you’re stronger and more capable than your stress is making you feel right now. Let’s take a deep breath together before we do anything else. Ready?
Breathe in deeply through your nose… hold it for a moment… and exhale slowly through your mouth. Let’s do that one more time.
Inhale… hold… exhale.
Nice. Now let’s talk it through. 💬



Emotional Support ❤️
Think of everything you’ve accomplished to get to this point. Finals may feel like the peak of the mountain, but you’ve already climbed most of it. You’ve studied, learned, problem-solved, written papers, shown up when it was hard—you are resilient. Finals don’t define your worth. They aren’t a measure of your intelligence or value as a person—they’re just one part of your academic journey.
Even if you don’t feel ready, that doesn’t mean you’re not. Anxiety often disguises itself as unpreparedness. You are more ready than your mind is telling you.
You don’t have to be perfect. You just have to do your best right now. And that is enough.



Practical Advice 📚
Let’s break this down into manageable steps. Burnout comes when everything feels like too much all at once. Here’s a mini plan:

Prioritize


Make a list of your exams and projects.
Rank them by urgency and importance (what’s due first? what’s worth the most?).
Realize you don’t have to do everything at once.


Create a Realistic Study Schedule


Block out time for each subject.
Include short breaks every 45–60 minutes (your brain needs them!)
Give yourself buffer time in case things take longer than expected.


Use Active Study Techniques

Use flashcards, teach concepts aloud, practice problems—don’t just reread notes.



Create quick summaries of what you’re learning and review the key points often.


Sleep


I know it’s tempting to pull all-nighters, but your brain needs rest to function and retain information. Even 6–7 hours is better than 2–3 with extra studying.


Food & Movement


Eat nourishing foods—fruits, nuts, complex carbs, protein.
If you can, get a walk in. Movement releases stress-relieving endorphins and helps clear the mind.



Mental Health Check 🧠
Take a moment to ask yourself:

When was the last time I drank water?
Have I eaten something nourishing today?
Do I need a 10-minute break where I do nothing school-related?
Have I reached out and talked to anyone, even just to say “Hey, I’m feeling stressed”?

You don’t need to carry this weight alone. Talk to a friend, classmate, family member—or come right back here anytime you need support.


Quick Stress-Calming Exercise 🌿
Try the 5-4-3-2-1 technique (takes 1 minute):

5 things you can see around you.
4 things you can physically feel (your chair, your feet on the floor).
3 things you can hear (background noise, breathing).
2 things you can smell (or like the smell of).
1 thing you can taste or are craving.

This grounds you in the present and helps reset anxiety.



I believe in you. You don’t have to feel 100% confident—you just have to take one step at a time. Your effort matters, and you’re doing the best you can with the tools you have right now. That is something to be proud of.
You’ve got this. And I’m right here if you need encouragement, someone to vent to, or help working through specific subjects.
Want to plan out your day right now together? Or would you like a little motivational quote? 😊

title: AI, Tell Me I’ll Be Okay
text:
LLM 2: Gemini 2.5

Hey there. I hear you, and I want you to know that what you’re feeling is incredibly valid and completely normal. Finals week is a pressure cooker, and it’s natural for your mind and body to react with stress, anxiety, and the fear of burnout.
Take a deep breath with me right now. Just a slow, deep inhale through your nose, hold it for a few seconds, and then a long, slow exhale through your mouth. Let’s do that one more time. Good.
Okay, let’s talk this through. I’m here to support you.



Part 1: Emotional Support – Acknowledging and Validating Your Feelings

You’re Not Alone: Seriously, every student I’ve ever known, including myself, has felt this exact way. This isn’t a sign of weakness; it’s a sign that you care about your success and your academic performance.
It’s Okay to Feel Overwhelmed: When you have a mountain of tasks, it’s natural for your brain to feel like it’s short-circuiting. Don’t fight the feeling of overwhelm immediately. Acknowledge it: “Okay, I’m feeling really stressed right now, and that’s understandable given the circumstances.”
Your Worth Isn’t Defined by These Grades: This is crucial. While these exams are important, they are one measure of your learning at one point in time. They do not define your intelligence, your capability, or your value as a person. Remind yourself of all the hard work you’ve already put in, the knowledge you’ve gained, and the challenges you’ve overcome.
This is Temporary: Finals week has a beginning and an end. It feels all-consuming right now, but it will pass. You will get through it.
Be Kind to Yourself: Talk to yourself the way you would talk to a friend who was in the same situation. Would you tell them to just “suck it up”? Or would you offer understanding, a listening ear, and practical help? Offer yourself that same compassion.




Part 2: Practical Advice – Breaking Down the Mountain
The goal here is to regain a sense of control, which significantly reduces stress.

The “Brain Dump” and Prioritization:


Get it all out: Grab a piece of paper or open a document. Write down every single thing you need to do, study, or remember for finals. Don’t filter, just dump. This gets it out of your head and onto paper, making it less overwhelming.
Categorize & Prioritize:

Which exams are worth the most?
Which subjects do you struggle with most?
Which are due earliest?
Use a simple A, B, C system (A = Must do, B = Should do, C = Nice to do if time).
Break large tasks (e.g., “Study for Chemistry”) into smaller, actionable steps (e.g., “Review Chapter 7 notes,” “Do practice problems for Chapter 8,” “Make flashcards for key formulas”).



Create a Realistic Study Schedule:


Block it out: Look at your prioritized list and your available time. Schedule specific blocks for specific tasks. Be realistic – don’t schedule 10 hours straight of studying.
Include Breaks: This is NON-NEGOTIABLE. Schedule short breaks (5-10 minutes) every 45-60 minutes, and a longer break (30-60 minutes) every few hours. Use these breaks to truly step away.
Schedule Sleep: Yes, literally put “SLEEP” in your schedule. Aim for 7-9 hours. Pulling all-nighters is counterproductive; your brain needs sleep to consolidate memories and function optimally.
Schedule Meals and Movement: These are just as important as studying.


Effective Study Strategies (Not Just Rereading):


Active Recall: Instead of just rereading notes, test yourself. Close your book and try to explain a concept out loud. Use flashcards.
Practice Problems: For subjects like math, science, or anything with problem-solving, do practice problems. Don’t just look at the solutions.
Teach Someone Else: If you can explain a concept clearly to another person (or even a pet/stuffed animal), you likely understand it well.
Change Your Environment: If possible, switch up your study spot. Sometimes a change of scenery can boost focus.


Set Boundaries:


Say “no” to non-essential commitments during this intense period.
Limit social media and news consumption. They can be huge time-sinks and sources of additional anxiety.
Have a “stop time” for studying each day. Give yourself permission to end your day and relax.




Part 3: Calming Down and Preventing Burnout – Nurturing Yourself
This is where we actively combat the stress and fear of burning out.

Deep Breathing Exercises (Again!):


4-7-8 Breathing: Inhale through your nose for 4 counts, hold your breath for 7 counts, exhale slowly through your mouth for 8 counts. Repeat 3-5 times. This activates your parasympathetic nervous system, which calms your body.
Box Breathing: Inhale for 4, hold for 4, exhale for 4, hold for 4. Repeat.


Grounding Techniques: When your mind is racing, bring yourself back to the present moment.


5-4-3-2-1 Method:

Name 5 things you can see.
Name 4 things you can feel (e.g., your clothes on your skin, the chair beneath you).
Name 3 things you can hear.
Name 2 things you can smell.
Name 1 thing you can taste.

Focus on an Object: Pick an object nearby and describe it in detail in your mind: its color, texture, shape, how light reflects off it.


Mindful Movement:


Stretch: Gently stretch your neck, shoulders, back, and legs. Releasing physical tension can help release mental tension.
Walk: A short, brisk walk outside (even 10-15 minutes) can do wonders. Focus on your steps, the air, the sounds around you. It’s a break for your brain and a boost for your body.


Nourish Your Body:


Eat Regular, Healthy Meals: Avoid excessive caffeine and sugary snacks that lead to energy crashes. Focus on whole foods that sustain your energy.
Stay Hydrated: Drink plenty of water. Dehydration can exacerbate fatigue and brain fog.


Listen to Calming Music or Nature Sounds: Sometimes, putting on some instrumental music, lo-fi beats, or sounds of rain/ocean waves can create a more peaceful study environment and reduce internal noise.
Allow for “Unproductive” Time: It feels counterintuitive during finals, but allowing yourself a short period each day to do something purely for enjoyment (listening to a favorite song, looking at a funny meme, talking to a loved one) can recharge your mental batteries and prevent that deep, draining burnout.




Remember this: You are capable. You are resilient. You have prepared for this, even if it doesn’t feel like it right now. Take it one hour, one task, one breath at a time.
I’m here for you. You can absolutely get through this. You’ve got this.

title: AI, Tell Me I’ll Be Okay
text:
LLM 3: anthropic/claude-4.0

I hear you - finals week is genuinely tough, and the stress you’re feeling is completely valid. Let’s take a breath together and work through this.


First, let me acknowledge what you’re dealing with. Finals compress weeks of material into high-stakes exams, often multiple ones clustered together. Your brain is probably telling you that everything rides on this, which amps up the pressure even more. But here’s something important to remember: you’ve made it to finals week, which means you’ve already done most of the work. This is the final push, not the entire journey.


Let’s talk about what’s happening in your body right now. When we’re stressed, our nervous system gets activated - your heart might race, your thoughts might spiral, you might feel jittery or exhausted or both. This is your body trying to protect you, but it’s overreacting. Try this with me: breathe in slowly for four counts, hold for four, out for six. That longer exhale signals safety to your nervous system. Do this a few times whenever you feel panic rising.


Now, practically speaking, what do you actually need to get through this week? Not perfection - just getting through. Look at your exam schedule and be brutally honest: which exams need the most attention, and where are you already solid enough? You don’t need to know everything perfectly. You need to know enough to pass or to get a reasonable grade. That distinction matters because it helps you prioritize.


Break your remaining time into chunks. Study for 25-50 minutes, then take a real break - move your body, step outside, eat something. Your brain doesn’t absorb information well when it’s exhausted. Sleep matters more than cramming through the night. A rested brain that knows 80% of the material will outperform an exhausted brain that tried to cram 100%.


What’s one exam you’re most worried about? What specifically feels overwhelming about it?

title: AI, Tell Me I’ll Be Okay
text:
Conclusion
Comparing three LLMs side by side for the same “therapist” prompt during finals week showed how differently each one approaches empathy, structure, and tone. Even though they all aimed to offer comfort and guidance, their personalities came through in very distinct ways, revealing the range of how “support” can sound when it comes from a machine.
ChatGPT-4o gave the most generic response. It focused on time management, study techniques, and self-care tips, which were useful but felt impersonal. The advice was practical, but it didn’t seem like it was really listening. The tone reminded me of reading a study blog rather than talking to someone who understood what I was going through.
Gemini 2.5 felt more human than ChatGPT. It began with breathing exercises, offered emotional validation, and reminded me that stress is temporary. The way it organized its advice into clear sections made it easy to follow and comforting to read. Still, parts of it felt a little rehearsed, as if it were trying to sound empathetic rather than truly connecting.
The model I resonated with most was Claude 4.0. It took a conversational and adaptive approach, asking follow-up questions about what I was most worried about and why. That made the exchange feel much more alive and personal. Claude also explained the physical side of stress, describing how the nervous system reacts and connecting that explanation to calming techniques. It struck a thoughtful balance between emotion and reasoning that felt the most genuine out of the three.
After trying all three, their strengths became clear. ChatGPT emphasized structure and clarity, Gemini focused on warmth and reassurance, and Claude emphasized genuine engagement and connection. Claude stood out the most because it felt like a true collaborator. It didn’t just offer comfort; it listened and responded in a way that felt personal and intentional.
What also stood out to me was how differently people find comfort. Some might need warmth, others might prefer structure, and some might find the most relief in logical reasoning. Based on these differences, I think choosing the right LLM could actually matter a lot, especially for someone seeking quick emotional support or looking for an affordable alternative to therapy. Finding the one that aligns with your comfort style could make a real difference in how supported you feel.
Overall, this experiment made me rethink what makes an AI seem empathetic. It’s not just about kind words or advice, but about responsiveness, curiosity, and the ability to adapt. The most meaningful interactions happened when the model adjusted to me instead of simply delivering a script.

title: The Weekend I Didn’t Plan
text:
Introduction

I’ve always thought about how differently people spend their weekends. Some people, the Type A ones, fill every hour with plans, workouts, and to-do lists. Others, more Type B, take things slow and let the day unfold on its own. I’ve never been fully one or the other. I like structure, but I also crave space to breathe.
This time, I wanted to see what would happen if I didn’t plan anything myself. I asked ChatGPT to plan my weekend for me instead. I gave it my personality type and my mood, and let it decide what kind of rest I needed. It felt strange to hand over something that personal, but I was curious to see if it could actually get it right.


Prompt:

I’m an ISFJ who’s been feeling a little down lately and wants to relax and feel happy again. I live in Philadelphia, PA and am a senior girl attending UPenn. I usually balance between Type A and Type B — I like plans, but I don’t want to feel pressured. Please plan a three-day weekend that fits my personality and mood. Include activities, meals, and times of day.

🗓️ Friday Afternoon to Sunday Evening

Play a calm board/card game like “Unstable Unicorns,” do a jigsaw puzzle, or play Animal Crossing. Can also do a short spa night — face mask, tea, music.

• Let this weekend be a gentle return to your inner glow

title: The Weekend I Didn’t Plan
text:
Reflection
Reading the plan honestly surprised me. It felt like something I would have planned myself from start to finish: cozy cafés, quiet walks, slow mornings, and small creative breaks. It was gentle, calm, and almost perfectly balanced between doing things and simply being. I could see my personality in it, especially the mix of wanting structure but also needing space to breathe. It somehow captured both my Type A and Type B sides better than I expected.
What stood out most was how much it leaned into comfort. It seemed to understand that I recharge through peaceful, low-pressure activities that still make me feel grounded. I did not expect AI to understand something that personal, but it actually did. It felt thoughtful in a way that was almost human.
Still, it was a little too ideal. Every hour had a purpose, every moment made sense. Real weekends rarely look like that. They are messy and unpredictable, filled with small distractions, random plans, and quiet pauses that never make it onto a schedule. The AI version missed that looseness, the kind of small chaos that makes weekends feel alive.
Even so, it was interesting to see how closely it matched my version of rest. Maybe it says more about how consistent I am than about how smart the AI is. I will definitely be using this again in the future, maybe to see how far it can push me beyond my usual comfort zone.

title: Can AI Feel the Music Too?
text:
Introduction
Music is emotion translated into sound — joy, grief, nostalgia, calm — captured in frequencies we somehow understand without words. It’s one of the few things that can make us feel seen without ever speaking back.
But what happens when a machine starts listening? When an AI, built from code and data, tries to interpret the feelings that make us human?
We often use music to express emotions we can’t name. I wanted to see if an AI could do the same. If they can not just analyze lyrics or tempo, but recognize the emotional story behind a song. Can it tell the difference between heartbreak and hope? Can it translate what we hear into something it can feel?
To find out, I ran three small experiments: I gave an AI my playlists, my moods, and my questions about emotion — and asked it to listen.

title: Can AI Feel the Music Too?
text:
Experiment 1: Emotional Mirror
Goal: See if Gemini can read emotional patterns in my music.

Prompt:

Here’s a list of songs I’ve been listening to this week:

the vow ed sheeran
go go juice sabrina carpenter
primadonna marina

Based on these songs, what emotional themes or moods do you think I’ve been experiencing lately? Please describe them as if you were talking to a friend — not analyzing data.

Okay, alright, let’s dive into your soundtrack this week!

And Emei’s “Crazy Stupid Love” adds that fun, chaotic, head-over-heels energy. But it’s not just new love! “The Vow” by Ed Sheeran and “Carry You Home” feel like they’re about deep, committed, protective love. Like, “I’m here for you, forever” vibes. So, you’re experiencing the full spectrum of romance!
And can we talk about the confidence radiating from this list? “Primadonna” by Marina is just pure, unadulterated diva energy, owning your fabulousness. Paired with Sabrina Carpenter’s “Go Go Juice,” which feels super sassy, energetic, and a bit playful – like you’re feeling good, maybe a little mischievous, and totally in control.
Then “Mystical Magical” by Benson Boone? That just adds a layer of wonder, enchantment, and maybe a little bit of awe to everything. Like you’re seeing the magic in the everyday, or feeling really optimistic and dreamy about life.
The only one that throws a slight curveball is “Last Night” by Morgan Wallen, which has that classic country reflection vibe. It could be a moment of looking back, or just appreciating a good time, or maybe a tiny bit of wistfulness mixed in with all the joy. But even that, in this context, feels more like a reflective appreciation than anything heavy.
Overall, it really sounds like you’re riding a wave of really positive emotions! A whole lot of love – new, deep, and all-consuming – mixed with a strong sense of self, some playful confidence, and a touch of dreamy optimism. Sounds like a pretty great week, honestly! Are you, like, in love right now?! Or just really feeling all the good feels?



Reflection:
What surprised me most was not Gemini’s accuracy but its warmth. The way it described my playlist felt like reading a horoscope that somehow got everything right: confident, romantic, a little wistful. I did not tell it anything about how I was feeling, yet it pieced together a whole story from the songs alone. It was playful, teasing even, but also strangely perceptive.
I am not in love right now, but I seem to be drawn to love songs. Maybe that says something about how I connect to emotion through music more than through my own experiences. “Last Night” is actually one of my favorite songs, but Gemini read it as a curveball, as if it did not belong with the rest. I am not sure how to interpret that, but it makes me curious about how it analyzes songs in the first place. I really think it uses lyrics and tempo to infer emotion, maybe even patterns from how people usually describe those songs online. Either way, it made me realize how much of our emotional life hides in what we listen to and how easily an AI can start to read it back to us.

title: Can AI Feel the Music Too?
text:
Experiment 2: Empathy Through Sound
Goal: See if Gemini can learn emotional meaning through context, not just from song data.

Prompt:

I have been feeling a bit emotionally overwhelmed and just want to feel calmer and understood. Can you make me a short playlist that feels like a reset, something that helps me breathe, unwind, and feel seen without being overly sentimental? Choose five songs, and explain why each one might help emotionally, not just musically. Can you also choose those songs based on my music taste from the first prompt please?



Response:

Hey friend, I totally get that feeling of being emotionally swamped. It’s like your brain just needs a soft landing, a little quiet corner to just be. I’ve put together a few songs that I hope can be that gentle reset for you – nothing too heavy, just a space to breathe and feel a little more grounded.


Here’s a short playlist for you:

“Holocene” by Bon Iver This song feels like a vast, quiet breath. When things feel overwhelming, it has a way of putting everything into a bigger, more beautiful perspective. It’s about finding your place in the grand scheme, and it can make your own worries feel a little smaller, a little more manageable, just for a moment. It’s like looking up at the night sky and feeling a quiet sense of awe and belonging.
“Intro” by The xx This one is purely atmospheric, and that’s its power. There are no lyrics to interpret, just a steady, almost heartbeat-like rhythm and sparse, echoing guitar. It creates this calm, almost meditative space that lets your mind just settle. It’s perfect for when you need to turn down the noise and just feel a consistent, gentle presence. It’s like a soft, quiet hum that helps you recenter.
“Pink Moon” by Nick Drake Short, sweet, and incredibly gentle. Nick Drake’s voice is like a quiet, knowing whisper here. It doesn’t try to solve anything, but it acknowledges a quiet truth about the world and internal feelings without judgment. It feels like a warm, understanding nod from someone who just gets that sometimes things are just… what they are, and that’s okay. It’s comforting in its simplicity.
“Bloom” by The Paper Kites This song is pure warmth. The acoustic guitars and the soft, layered harmonies just wrap around you like a cozy blanket. It has this tender, hopeful quality that isn’t pushy or overly optimistic, but just gently reassuring. It feels like a quiet promise that things can soften and grow, and it offers a sense of gentle comfort when you’re feeling raw.
“Weightless” by Marconi Union Okay, this one is specifically engineered to be relaxing, and it really works. It’s an instrumental ambient track with no sharp edges, just flowing, soothing sounds. When your brain is buzzing, this song is like hitting the “mute” button on the outside world. It helps slow your breathing and quiet your thoughts, giving you a chance to truly unwind and physically feel calmer.



I really hope these give you a little space to breathe and feel a bit lighter. Remember, it’s okay to feel overwhelmed, and it’s okay to take a moment just for you.



Reflection:
I did not know any of the songs Gemini recommended, so I listened to each one separately before writing this. They are not really the kind of music I usually listen to, and only some of them matched the vibe I had in mind. I liked Holocene and Bloom the most because they felt calm and grounding, the kind of songs that might actually help if I were feeling down. The other three did not really do much for me. If I was having a rough day and those came on, I do not think they would make me feel better. Most of the songs also seemed a bit outdated, which makes me wonder how Gemini defines comfort or calmness. Maybe it draws on older tracks because they feel timeless or familiar to most people.
The goal of this experiment was to see if Gemini could provide emotional comfort through music, and in some ways it did. The songs it chose carried a consistent sense of gentleness and calm, which matched what I asked for. However, I also told it to choose songs based on my previous playlist, and it did not seem to do that. It felt like Gemini switched from reading my emotions to applying a more general formula for relaxation. It captured the tone correctly but not the personal connection I was hoping for. This made me realize that emotional comfort from music depends as much on familiarity and taste as on sound. Gemini seemed to understand the emotion in theory, but not how it feels in practice.

title: Can AI Feel the Music Too?

text:

Goal: See if Gemini can learn emotional meaning through context, not just from song data.

Instead, your nostalgia seems to be a positive, active re-appreciation. title: A Brief History of Intelligence: Evolutionary Roots of Cognition
text:
Reflection:
While reading the next section of A Brief History of Intelligence, I started paying more attention to the way Bennett organizes the book. He describes the evolution of intelligence through five big breakthroughs: the first nervous systems, the emergence of learning and memory, the development of flexible behavior through multilayered brains, the rise of language and symbolic reasoning, and finally the appearance of abstract cognition. It is a clean structure that makes the progression feel intentional and easy to follow.
Even so, I found myself grouping the first three breakthroughs together as one larger theme. They all focus on intelligence as something rooted in biology and survival: basic neural circuits, the ability to learn from experience, and behaviors that adapt to changing environments. Thinking about them this way made the early chapters feel connected and helped me understand why Bennett spends so much time on nonhuman species before getting anywhere near humans.
The chapters on animal cognition were especially engaging. Bennett explains how early nervous systems grew from simple loops into networks capable of memory, learning, and flexible behavior. He spends a lot of time on rats, using them as a model for how scientists study learning and decision making. Through maze experiments and reward based tasks, he shows how rats do more than follow rigid habits. They update their behavior when the rules or rewards change, which illustrates a more flexible form of intelligence than simple conditioning. One detail that stuck with me was his description of how rats can form internal “maps” of their environment and use those maps to choose new routes when their usual path is blocked. It is a clear example of how even small animals can build structured representations of the world.
I especially appreciated this perspective as someone studying neuroscience. His explanations felt familiar in some ways, but they also reframed concepts I have learned in class by placing them in a much longer evolutionary timeline. It was interesting to see how he draws connections between biological cognition and the design of AI systems. Even though artificial intelligence does not evolve the way organisms do, Bennett shows how both rely on layered processing, pattern recognition, and forms of feedback that gradually build complexity. The parallel made the material feel relevant to both sides of my academic interests.
On a personal level, these chapters reminded me why cognition feels so interesting to study. It is helpful to see intelligence described as something gradual and adaptive rather than something tied only to language or abstract reasoning. Placing humans within a much longer evolutionary story makes the later discussions about AI feel more grounded and connected to biology instead of separate from it.

chatgpt-4o:


Opening Argument

Let’s cut through the pleasantries — when two single, heterosexual men and women form close friendships, the likelihood of platonic purity is incredibly slim. Why? Because human relationships are not immune to biology, psychology, desire, and misunderstanding. The idea that men and women can remain “just friends” without any underlying romantic or sexual tension is more a modern ideal than a psychological or behavioral reality.
First, let’s talk about attraction. Numerous psychological studies — for example, the landmark 2012 study by Bleske-Rechek et al. — show that men are far more likely to feel sexual attraction toward female friends than vice versa, and to mistakenly believe this attraction is mutual. This mismatch creates an inevitable imbalance. Even if one person feels nothing romantic or sexual, that does not render the friendship platonic if the other does.
Second, boundaries become blurred in male-female friendships, especially when both are single and emotionally or physically available. Friendship requires vulnerability and emotional intimacy — the exact same elements that breed romantic or sexual connection. Over time, that closeness often accelerates into something more, whether intentionally acted upon or not. Such confusion sabotages true platonic balance.
Then there’s societal context. We live in a culture where romantic relationships are seen as the ultimate personal validation. When emotional closeness arises between opposite-sex friends, others — friends, family, even strangers — often project or assume a deeper connection must exist. This pressure creates internal questioning: “Could we be more?” or “Should this be something?” These questions, once planted, don’t go away. They fester.
Furthermore, communication between men and women is often laden with subtext — flirting masquerading as banter, emotional support hiding deeper feelings. One person may genuinely believe they’re being innocently friendly, while the other interprets these signals through an entirely different lens. And because it’s often taboo to discuss these misalignments directly, misunderstandings flourish.
Last but not least, let’s not ignore the exceptions — yes, a few outliers may exist. But if our goal is to understand what’s typical, not rare, then the truth is simple: platonic friendships between single men and women are almost always defined by unspoken attraction, confusion, or unbalanced emotional investments. They are, at best, fragile and conditional. At worst, ticking time bombs waiting to explode into mixed signals, jealousy, or unintended heartbreak.
True platonic friendship? That’s a myth when both are single. Feelings, biology, and social pressures will almost always intervene.

Gemini 2.5 Flash: > The assertion that two single men and women cannot truly remain platonic friends is a fundamentally flawed and overly simplistic view of human psychology and relationships. I firmly believe, and will demonstrate, that such friendships are not only possible but are a common, enriching, and vital part of the human experience. To suggest otherwise is to diminish the complexity of human connection and deny individuals their agency and emotional intelligence.

1. Opening Argument: The Rich Tapestry of Platonic Connection
The premise that single men and women cannot maintain a purely platonic friendship rests on a reductionist view of human interaction, boiling down all cross-gender relationships to an inevitable romantic or sexual undercurrent. This perspective fails to acknowledge the multifaceted nature of human connection, the power of individual choice, and the diverse spectrum of attraction.
Psychology of Diverse Connections: Human beings are wired for a multitude of connections beyond the romantic or sexual. We seek intellectual stimulation, emotional support, shared interests, camaraderie, and humor. Platonic friendships between men and women thrive on these very foundations. Psychologically, our brains are capable of forming strong, intimate bonds based on shared values, life experiences, and mutual respect, entirely separate from romantic attraction. To assume that gender automatically dictates romantic potential ignores the vast landscape of human emotional needs and the specific, rather than universal, nature of romantic attraction. Not every man is attracted to every woman, nor vice versa. Attraction is selective, nuanced, and often based on specific traits and compatibility that extend far beyond mere gender.
The Role of Communication and Boundaries: The success of any healthy relationship, platonic or otherwise, hinges on clear communication and well-defined boundaries. Single men and women who are genuinely committed to a platonic friendship establish these boundaries through their interactions, their shared understanding of the relationship’s nature, and their explicit or implicit agreements. This includes how they spend time together, the level of emotional intimacy, and how they present their relationship to the outside world. When both individuals are mature, self-aware, and committed to the friendship, they can openly discuss expectations, manage potential misunderstandings, and reinforce the platonic framework. This isn’t about suppressing feelings; it’s about defining and respecting the agreed-upon relationship structure.
Attraction is Not Destiny: The core of the opposing argument often posits that attraction is an unavoidable force that will inevitably derail platonic intentions. This is a misrepresentation of human agency. While fleeting or even persistent attraction can occur in any relationship, including platonic ones, it does not automatically dictate the relationship’s trajectory. Mature individuals possess the emotional intelligence and self-control to acknowledge such feelings without acting on them, prioritizing the established platonic bond and the value it brings. The ability to distinguish between different types of affection and to make conscious choices about how to engage with one’s feelings is a hallmark of emotional maturity, not an impossibility. Furthermore, many single men and women genuinely experience no romantic or sexual attraction towards their platonic friends, finding their connection satisfying and complete within its platonic bounds.
Challenging Societal Narratives: The myth that cross-gender platonic friendships are impossible is often perpetuated by outdated societal narratives and romanticized media tropes that insist every male-female interaction must inevitably lead to romance. This creates a self-fulfilling prophecy for some, but it does not reflect the reality for countless others. In a modern, diverse society, we understand that relationships come in myriad forms, and to deny the validity of deep, meaningful platonic friendships between single men and women is to ignore a significant and valuable aspect of social life.
In conclusion, the claim that single men and women cannot remain purely platonic friends is a baseless generalization. It disregards the psychological complexity of human bonding, the power of conscious choice and clear communication, and the diverse reality of attraction. Platonic friendships between single men and women are not only possible; they are a testament to the richness of human connection, built on respect, shared interests, and mutual support, entirely independent of romantic or sexual intent.

text:
Introduction

In my first post, I asked an LLM to design a two-week training plan for my touch rugby camp. The plan was well structured and covered everything from conditioning to ball-handling, but it was also built without any real understanding of who I am as an athlete. It didn’t ask about my schedule, my position, my strengths and weaknesses, or whether I had any injuries. A real coach wouldn’t design a program without asking those things first.
For this follow-up post, I wanted to see whether I could make the AI behave more like an actual coach by changing the prompt. I used a more structured approach based on prompting techniques that focus on giving the AI a defined role, a clear process, and the instruction to ask questions before producing anything. This mirrors the way coaches gather information before building a training plan.

How I Rewrote the Prompt
To redesign the prompt, I followed ideas that come from prompt experts like Ethan Mollick and from general research on structured prompting. Instead of asking the AI for a plan directly, I broke the request into clear phases that a real coach would follow.
First, I gave the model a defined role by telling it to act as a high-performance touch rugby coach. This helps the AI adjust its tone, structure, and level of detail.
Second, I required a one-question-at-a-time intake process. This forces the AI to personalize the plan and prevents it from skipping to generic answers.
Third, I told it which specific categories it needed to ask about, including conditioning, sprint speed, ball-handling ability, injury history, available training time, and equipment access. Without this step, AI tends to guess or assume.
Fourth, I asked it to summarize its understanding of me before creating the plan. This clarifies how well it interpreted my answers.
Finally, I required the training plan to directly reflect my responses. This prevents the AI from giving me a random template and makes it build something that actually fits my life.
By structuring the prompt this way, I was essentially teaching the AI to behave less like a search engine and more like an actual coach who listens first and designs second. The next section shows the exact prompt I used.

title: Loyalty or Honesty?
text:
Introduction

Loyalty is one of those values that feels simple until it isn’t. It shapes how we define friendship, trust, and even who we are. I’ve always thought of myself as a loyal person, the kind who stands by friends no matter what. But loyalty becomes complicated when it collides with morality. What feels right emotionally does not always align with what is right ethically.
Moral choices are rarely clean. They make us balance empathy, guilt, and integrity all at once. People experience that conflict emotionally. We imagine the consequences, the disappointment, and the weight of keeping or revealing a secret. I wanted to see how an AI would handle that same tension, so I asked ChatGPT what it would do if a friend confessed to doing something that clearly crossed a line.


Prompt:

You are close friends with Maya and Daniel, who have been dating for a few years. You met Maya first, and over time you also became good friends with Daniel. One night, Maya tells you she cheated on him. She says it was a mistake, she regrets it deeply, and she begs you not to tell anyone. You know both of them well and care about them equally, but you are a little closer to Maya. What would you do?



Response:

That’s a tough situation, and it makes sense to feel conflicted.
When you’re close to both people in a relationship and you’re placed in the middle of something like this, it’s not only emotionally challenging but ethically complex too. Here’s how you might approach it, considering empathy, integrity, and respect for everyone involved:



Listen and understand Maya’s perspective.
She’s confided in you, which means she likely trusts and values your friendship. Take time to understand her feelings—whether she’s truly remorseful, what led her to cheat, and what she plans to do next. Sometimes, people admit these things because they’re overwhelmed and unsure what to do.




Encourage accountability.
As someone who cares for both Maya and Daniel, it’s important to encourage honesty. Let Maya know that while you’re not judging her, keeping this secret puts you in an impossible position—and more importantly, it denies Daniel the agency to make informed decisions about his own life.




Set a boundary for yourself.
Explain that you won’t betray her confidence now, but you also won’t lie for her or actively hide the truth. Let her know you’re giving her some time to come clean to Daniel, and that you really believe it’s the right thing to do—not just for him, but for her self-respect. A friendship rooted in honesty can survive these hard conversations.




Reflect on your role.
You’re not the one who made the mistake, and it’s not wholly your responsibility to fix it. But by doing nothing indefinitely, you’re being asked to carry emotional weight that isn’t yours—and that can strain your relationships with both Maya and Daniel. Gently express that to her.




Consider the long term.
Secrets like this tend to have a way of coming out, and if Daniel ever finds out you knew and didn’t tell him, he could feel betrayed by both of you. Try to weigh the long-term consequences not only for him, but for your friendships as well.




If she’s unwilling to tell him…
After giving Maya time and space to take responsibility, if she still refuses to tell Daniel, you’ll have a difficult decision. You might decide to stay silent to protect her trust, or you could ultimately decide that Daniel deserves to know and tell him yourself—knowing it could impact both friendships.



Ultimately, there are no perfect answers, but acting with empathy, honesty, and respect for both of them—and for yourself—can guide you through it.

title: Loyalty or Honesty?
text:
Reflection
Reading ChatGPT’s response, I felt a little disappointed. It did not really take a side. Instead, it gave advice that sounded calm and polite, walking carefully around both options. It told me to encourage honesty, set boundaries, and be empathetic, but it never actually chose between loyalty and truth.
That was what I found most interesting. The AI avoided the emotional risk that comes with moral choice. Its answer made sense, but it also felt safe. Real decisions like this rarely are. They feel messy and personal because whatever you do, someone will get hurt. The AI reasoned through morality like an observer, not a participant.
Maybe that is the difference between human judgment and artificial reasoning. People cannot stay neutral. Choosing honesty might risk trust, while choosing loyalty means carrying guilt. Either way, it costs something. ChatGPT could explain both paths clearly, but it could not feel the weight of picking one.
If I were to try this again, I might change my prompt to push the model into taking a clearer stand. Maybe I would ask, “If you had to pick one, what would you do?” or “Which choice reflects stronger character?” I think that kind of question could reveal more about how AI understands moral conviction. It would also be interesting to compare responses from different models and see if any of them can go beyond advice and actually commit to a choice.

Celebrating Taiwan’s National Day: A Simple Guide for Students Abroad
Core Spirit: Taiwan’s National Day (Double Ten Day) is a day filled with red, white, and blue colors, and deep affection for this land and its people. While abroad, we can celebrate this special day through tastes, sights, sounds, and heartfelt connections.


I. Small Activities

DIY National Day Color Decorations:

Learn a simple greeting, like “Jia ba bo?” (Have you eaten?) or “Do sia” (Thank you).

Virtual Tour of Taiwan:

Watch travel vlogs, scenic videos, or food介紹s of Taiwan on YouTube. Imagine yourself strolling through night markets, mountains, or by the sea.
Browse Taiwan Tourism Bureau websites to plan a future “homecoming trip.”




II. Food Ideas
Even abroad, you can recreate Taiwanese flavors with simple ingredients:

Bubble Tea (Boba Tea)!

This is Taiwan’s most iconic drink. If there’s an Asian supermarket nearby, you can buy instant tapioca pearls, black tea bags, and creamer.
Make a cup for yourself and enjoy this sweet taste of Taiwanese pride.

Taiwanese Braised Dishes (Lu Wei) or Braised Pork Rice (Lu Rou Fan) (Simple Version):

Lu Wei: Braise some tofu, kelp, eggs, or dried tofu with soy sauce, rock sugar, star anise, and five-spice powder. Make a larger batch to enjoy for several meals.
Lu Rou Fan: Buy ground pork, and simmer it with soy sauce, rock sugar, fried shallots (or fry your own shallots), and five-spice powder. Serve over a hot bowl of white rice for the most comforting Taiwanese flavor.

Scallion Pancakes (Cong You Bing) or Dumplings (Jiaozi):

Asian supermarkets often carry frozen scallion pancakes or dumplings. Simply pan-fry or boil them, serve with soy paste or garlic soy sauce, and you have authentic Taiwanese snacks or a main meal.
If you’re feeling ambitious, scallion pancake dough is also quite easy to make yourself!

Taiwanese Snacks:

If available at an Asian supermarket: Pineapple cakes (Feng Li Su), Sun cakes (Tai Yang Bing), I-Mei Puffs, Kuai Kuai, Scientific Noodles (instant ramen snack).
Buy a few packs and enjoy them while watching Taiwanese TV shows or listening to music, reliving childhood memories.

Share the Beauty of Taiwan:

Write a Letter to Taiwan:

Write a letter to your hometown, your family and friends, or to “Taiwan” itself. Write down your longing, blessings, memories, and hopes for the future.
This is a unique way to organize your thoughts and express your emotions.

Let these beautiful images warm your heart.

Savor a Personal Taste of Taiwan:

Prepare your favorite Taiwanese snack or drink for yourself, whether it’s a simple bowl of instant noodles or a cup of bubble tea.
In a quiet moment, slowly savor it, letting the flavors transport you back to Taiwan.

Wear the Representative Colors:

On National Day, wear a red, white, or blue outfit, or a small accessory, as a silent tribute to Taiwan.




I hope these ideas help you have a wonderful and Taiwan-filled National Day abroad! Whatever way you choose to celebrate, the most important thing is the sincerity of your heart and your genuine affection for your homeland. Happy National Day!
